for f in ['/workspace/tmp/scogs_animals.zip','/workspace/tmp/scogs_fungi.zip']:

import sys, zipfile
zpath = sys.argv[1]
z = zipfile.ZipFile(zpath)
out = []
for name in z.namelist():
    if not name.endswith('.mldist'):
        continue
    text = z.read(name).decode('ascii')
    lines = [line.strip() for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    if not lines:
        continue
    n = int(lines[0].split()[0])
    vals = []
    for line in lines[1:]:
        parts = line.split()
        for tok in parts[1:1+n]:
            vals.append(float(tok))
    total = sum(vals)
    mean = total / (n * (n - 1))
    out.append((name, mean))
out.sort()
for name, mean in out:
    print(f\"{name}\\t{mean:.12g}\")
'''

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Paired group comparison for BUSCO single-copy ortholog phylogenetics.

This script extracts BOTH `scogs_animals.zip` and `scogs_fungi.zip`,
computes the requested per-ortholog metric on every ortholog, and emits
both per-group summaries AND the cross-group Mann-Whitney U + p-value
in a single invocation. It exists to address timeouts the agent hits
when re-running per-group batches separately.

Why this is faster than calling phykit_batch twice:

- For metrics derivable from alignment columns alone (parsimony_informative,
  rcv, gap_percentage), it uses Biopython directly — no subprocess fork
  per file. ~100x speedup on 500 alignments.

  patristic_distances, evolutionary_rate), it spawns one phykit process

representation.shell_command:
set -eu
python3 - "$(inputs.animals_archive.path)" animals "$(inputs.fungi_archive.path)" fungi > per_tree_means.tsv <<'PY'
import os, pathlib, subprocess, sys, tempfile, zipfile

out = []
work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='scogs_patristic_')
for zpath, group in [(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]), (sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4])]:
    z = zipfile.ZipFile(zpath)
    tree_names = [n for n in z.namelist() if n.endswith('.treefile')]
    group_dir = os.path.join(work, group)
    os.makedirs(group_dir, exist_ok=True)
    for name in tree_names:
        path = os.path.join(group_dir, pathlib.Path(name).name)
        with open(path, 'wb') as fh:
            fh.write(z.read(name))
        proc = subprocess.run(['phykit', 'patristic_distances', path, '-v'],
                              capture_output=True, text=True)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            continue
        vals = []
        for line in proc.stdout.splitlines():
            parts = line.split('\t')
            if not parts:
                continue
            try:
                vals.append(float(parts[-1]))
            except ValueError:
                pass
        if vals:
            out.append((group, name, sum(vals) / len(vals)))

out.sort()
for group, name, mean in out:
    print(f"{group}\t{name}\t{mean:.12g}")
PY

set -eu
python3 - "/jetstream2/scratch/main/jobs/79182662/inputs/dataset_08ec74c0-a79d-4683-b47a-f894a91d31f7.dat" animals "/jetstream2/scratch/main/jobs/79182662/inputs/dataset_feeb634d-25aa-4b7f-b5e9-96db97e1de1f.dat" fungi > per_tree_means.tsv <<'PY'
import os, pathlib, subprocess, sys, tempfile, zipfile

out = []
work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='scogs_patristic_')
for zpath, group in [(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]), (sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4])]:
    z = zipfile.ZipFile(zpath)
    tree_names = [n for n in z.namelist() if n.endswith('.treefile')]
    group_dir = os.path.join(work, group)
    os.makedirs(group_dir, exist_ok=True)
    for name in tree_names:
        path = os.path.join(group_dir, pathlib.Path(name).name)
        with open(path, 'wb') as fh:
            fh.write(z.read(name))
        proc = subprocess.run(['phykit', 'patristic_distances', path, '-v'],
                              capture_output=True, text=True)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            continue
        vals = []
        for line in proc.stdout.splitlines():
            parts = line.split('\t')
            if not parts:
                continue
            try:
                vals.append(float(parts[-1]))
            except ValueError:
                pass
        if vals:
            out.append((group, name, sum(vals) / len(vals)))

out.sort()
for group, name, mean in out:
    print(f"{group}\t{name}\t{mean:.12g}")
